title: FMCG — DPP characteristics
description: Field specifications for the FMCG Digital Product Passport, shaped for UNTP's credentialSubject.characteristics extension point. Economic operators and facility identifiers are carried by the UNTP envelope and are deliberately absent here.

productName.title: Product Name
productName.description: Commercial product name or trade designation

brandName.title: Brand Name
brandName.description: Brand or trademark under which the product is marketed
brandName.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

gtin.title: GTIN / Barcode
gtin.description: Global Trade Item Number (EAN-13 or GTIN-14) barcode identifier
gtin.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. netContentValue.title: Net Content
netContentValue.description: Net weight (g) or volume (ml) of the product

netContentUnit.title: Net Content Unit
netContentUnit.description: Unit of measurement for net content

ingredientsList.title: Ingredients List
ingredientsList.description: Full INCI ingredient list (cosmetics) or composition disclosure (detergents) in descending order of concentration

allergens.title: Allergens
allergens.description: Declared fragrance allergens present above 0.001% (leave-on) or 0.01% (rinse-off) per 2023 update covering 80+ allergens
allergens.x-citationNote: Lists substances restricted in cosmetics subject to conditions, and where a listed fragrance allergen is present above the annex threshold its name must appear in the Art. 19(1)(g) ingredient list ON THE PACKAGING. The duty is discharged by that pack labelling, not by publishing an allergen list here.

fragrances.title: Fragrances
fragrances.description: Named fragrances present in the product above disclosure threshold
fragrances.x-citationNote: It requires the ingredient list on the container or packaging, and allows perfume and aromatic compositions to be given as 'parfum' or 'aroma' rather than itemised. So the Regulation deliberately does NOT require a full fragrance breakdown; publishing one exceeds the duty.

preservatives.title: Preservatives
preservatives.description: Preservative substances with CAS numbers, mandatory disclosure for cosmetics and detergents
preservatives.x-citationNote: It is the positive list of preservatives permitted in cosmetics, with their conditions and maximum concentrations. It is a composition restriction — use only what is listed, within its limits — and the disclosure that follows is the Art. 19(1)(g) ingredient list on the pack.

svhcPresence.title: Substances of Very High Concern
svhcPresence.description: SVHC substances present above 0.1% w/w with name, CAS number, concentration range, and safe use instructions
svhcPresence.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

colorants.title: Colorants
colorants.description: Colorants used in the product, identified by CI (Colour Index) number
colorants.x-citationNote: It is the positive list of permitted colorants. Like Annex V it restricts what may be used rather than requiring a separate declaration; the ingredient list on the packaging is where colorants are disclosed.

nanomaterials.title: Nanomaterials
nanomaterials.description: Nanomaterials present in the product, labelled with [nano] per Cosmetics Regulation
nanomaterials.x-citationNote: Two duties apply and neither is a passport. Nanomaterials must be notified electronically to the Commission before placing on the market, and in the Art. 19(1)(g) ingredient list a nanomaterial's name is followed by '(nano)' ON THE PACK.

clpHazardClassification.title: CLP Hazard Classification
clpHazardClassification.description: Full CLP classification including hazard class, category, and signal word
clpHazardClassification.x-citationNote: CLP's operative duty is to classify the substance or mixture and to communicate the resulting classification through the LABEL and the safety data sheet. Publishing the classification as product data neither creates nor discharges that obligation.

ghsPictograms.title: GHS Pictograms
ghsPictograms.description: GHS hazard pictogram codes applicable to the product (GHS01 through GHS09)
ghsPictograms.x-citationNote: Hazard pictograms are label elements: CLP requires them to be affixed on the package. A passport copy repeats the information without discharging the labelling duty.

hazardStatements.title: Hazard Statements
hazardStatements.description: H-code hazard statements describing the nature of the hazard (e.g. H315 Causes skin irritation)
hazardStatements.x-citationNote: Hazard statements (H-phrases) are CLP label elements, required on the package alongside the pictogram, signal word and precautionary statements. The label is the vehicle.

precautionaryStatements.title: Precautionary Statements
precautionaryStatements.description: P-code precautionary statements describing recommended safety measures
precautionaryStatements.x-citationNote: Precautionary statements (P-phrases) are CLP label elements required on the package. Reproducing them here is useful to a reader but is not how the duty is met.

firstAidInstructions.title: First Aid Instructions
firstAidInstructions.description: First aid measures in case of exposure: skin contact, eye contact, ingestion, inhalation
firstAidInstructions.x-citationNote: GPSR Art. 9 requires safety information and instructions to ACCOMPANY the product where needed for safe use. The duty is discharged by supplying them with the product; a passport copy is a convenience.

ufi.title: Unique Formula Identifier (UFI)
ufi.description: 16-character UFI code for poison centre notification, mandatory for hazardous mixtures
ufi.x-citationNote: The unique formula identifier exists to link a product to the mixture information notified to the bodies appointed under CLP Art. 45 for emergency health response. The duties are to NOTIFY those bodies and to place the UFI on the label; publishing it in a passport does neither.

carbonFootprint.title: Carbon Footprint
carbonFootprint.description: Product carbon footprint in kg CO2-eq per functional unit, calculated per EU Product Environmental Footprint methodology
carbonFootprint.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

waterFootprint.title: Water Footprint
waterFootprint.description: Water scarcity footprint in litres per functional unit, per ISO 14046
waterFootprint.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

biodegradability.title: Biodegradability
biodegradability.description: Ultimate aerobic biodegradability of surfactants and organic content, including test method and degradation percentage
biodegradability.x-citationNote: Reg (EC) 648/2004 is the PREVIOUS Detergents Regulation, superseded by Reg (EU) 2026/405 which applies from 23 Sep 2029. Its surfactant biodegradability rule is a market-placement condition — the surfactant must pass, with the evidence held in the technical documentation — not a duty to publish the result.

aquaticToxicity.title: Aquatic Toxicity
aquaticToxicity.x-citationNote: Aquatic hazard is a CLP classification, communicated through the hazard statement and pictogram on the LABEL and through the safety data sheet. CLP requires no separate publication of toxicity data as product information.

ecolabelCriticalDilutionVolume.title: Critical Dilution Volume (CDV)
ecolabelCriticalDilutionVolume.description: Critical dilution volume per wash load in litres -- key metric for EU Ecolabel detergent certification
ecolabelCriticalDilutionVolume.x-citationNote: The EU Ecolabel is a VOLUNTARY scheme. Reg (EC) 66/2010 has a real CELEX, so citing it looks legislative while imposing no obligation on a product that does not seek the label. Critical dilution volume is a criterion for award, not a legal requirement.

packagingRecycledContent.title: Packaging Recycled Content (%)
packagingRecycledContent.description: Percentage of post-consumer recycled content in packaging. PPWR targets: 30% by 2030, 65% by 2040 for PET
packagingRecycledContent.x-citationNote: It sets minimum recycled content for plastic packaging from 1 Jan 2030, with the calculation and verification methodology to be set by delegated act under Art. 7(8). The duty binds the packaging, not the packaged product, and is not in force.

packagingRecyclabilityGrade.title: Packaging Recyclability Grade
packagingRecyclabilityGrade.description: Recyclability performance grade per PPWR: A (highest) to E (not recyclable)
packagingRecyclabilityGrade.x-citationNote: Recyclability grades A-E depend on design-for-recycling criteria set by delegated acts under Art. 6(4), not adopted, and apply from 2030. Nothing today lets the grade be computed or requires it.

packagingWeight.title: Packaging Weight (g)
packagingWeight.description: Total packaging weight in grams (primary + secondary packaging)
packagingWeight.x-citationNote: Packaging weight is an input to the Art. 10 minimisation assessment, which applies from 2030 against the Annex IV criteria under a delegated methodology. No in-force provision requires declaring it, and the duty attaches to the packaging rather than to this product.

packagingToProductRatio.title: Packaging-to-Product Ratio
packagingToProductRatio.description: Ratio of packaging weight to product weight, for empty space minimization assessment
packagingToProductRatio.x-citationNote: It requires packaging to be minimised to the weight and volume necessary for functionality, safety and hygiene, and caps empty space for grouped, transport and e-commerce packaging from 2030. The ratio expresses that future assessment; it is not a mandated declaration.

recommendedDosage.title: Recommended Dosage
recommendedDosage.description: Recommended dosage or usage amount per application (e.g. 30ml per wash load, pea-sized amount)
recommendedDosage.x-citationNote: Art. 19 requires particulars concerning precautions for use to appear on the container and packaging. Usage or dosage guidance is delivered through that pack labelling rather than as published product data.

shelfLifeMonths.title: Shelf Life (Months)
shelfLifeMonths.description: Product shelf life in months. For cosmetics with shelf life >30 months, Period After Opening (PAO) symbol is used instead
shelfLifeMonths.x-citationNote: Reg (EU) 1169/2011 Art. 19(1) concerns food information; where a date of minimum durability or use-by date is required it must appear ON THE FOOD LABEL. A shelf-life duration in months is a derived figure, and the labelling duty is discharged on pack.

storageConditions.title: Storage Conditions
storageConditions.description: Recommended storage conditions: temperature, humidity, light exposure
storageConditions.x-citationNote: GPSR requires the instructions and safety information needed for safe use to accompany the product. Storage guidance is part of that accompanying information rather than mandated passport data.

batchLotNumber.title: Batch / Lot Number
batchLotNumber.description: Batch or lot identification number for traceability and recall purposes

certifications.title: Certifications
certifications.description: Applicable environmental, quality, and ethical certifications held by the product
certifications.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

euEcolabelLicenseNumber.title: EU Ecolabel License Number
euEcolabelLicenseNumber.description: EU Ecolabel license number if certified (format: XX/XXX/XXXX)
euEcolabelLicenseNumber.x-citationNote: A licence number exists only where the manufacturer has voluntarily applied for and been awarded the EU Ecolabel. Nothing requires seeking it, so nothing requires publishing it.

organicCertificationBody.title: Organic Certification Body
organicCertificationBody.description: Name and code of the organic certification body (e.g. Ecocert, ICEA)
organicCertificationBody.x-citationNote: Organic certification under Reg (EU) 2018/848 applies to operators who choose to place products on the market as organic; the control body's code then appears in the labelling that regime prescribes. It is conditional on a voluntary claim, not a general duty.

disposalInstructions.title: Disposal Instructions
disposalInstructions.description: Consumer-facing disposal and recycling instructions for both product residue and packaging

refillAvailability.title: Refill Availability
refillAvailability.description: Whether the product is available in refill format (concentrate, refill pouch, refill station)
refillAvailability.x-citationNote: It concerns refill systems and the requirements that apply where an operator offers one. Offering refill is a business choice, not an obligation, so declaring its availability is voluntary information rather than compliance data.

returnSchemeParticipation.title: Return Scheme Participation
returnSchemeParticipation.description: Whether packaging participates in a deposit-return scheme (DRS) per PPWR
returnSchemeParticipation.x-citationNote: PPWR Arts. 44-48 place extended-producer-responsibility and take-back duties on producers and Member States, and Art. 50 requires deposit-and-return systems by 1 Jan 2029. These bind the producer's registration and the national scheme; a participation flag on a product passport neither creates nor discharges them.
